Replace ALL robot arms, mechanical joints, bases and tooltips with ONE coherent illustrative subject: a natural-looking cat standing sideways on a lower ledge, placing its raised near front paw on the edge of a higher windowsill. This cat is the SUBJECT BEING PAINTED, never a drawing machine. Preserve the polished white, navy, teal/amber diagram style, 1536x1024 landscape layout, large legible English typography, three numbered columns, and bottom pixel-review feedback. Recompose drawings and labels as needed to avoid clutter.
Title exactly: 'AUTHORED GEOMETRY → EDITABLE PAINT'. Subtitle exactly: 'The artist chooses the form. Mathematics supports construction.'
Column 1: '1 Author the model'. Show a recognizable anatomically plausible side-view cat as a light grey construction drawing, tail curved, all limbs naturally placed. Mark shoulder, elbow, wrist and paw on the raised near front leg with small landmark dots; thin segment guides indicate the authored chain, no mechanical hardware. A red cross lies at the raised paw contact on the higher sill. Use only these callouts: 'Landmarks', 'Proportions', 'Joint limits', 'Contact target'. Cat body length/head size proportion guide; leg joints follow plausible feline orientation.
Column 2: '2 Solve & compile'. Top: three separate compact method cards, with NO arrows connecting them and a small heading 'Choose methods as needed': 'IK.ts / FABRIK' with sublabel 'Reach the contact target'; 'Bezier.js' with 'Smooth contours'; 'Clipper2' with 'Clip protected areas'. The diagram must NOT imply all three libraries are mandatory or a serial pipeline. Below: same cat pose, raised front leg joint chain overlaid in teal, paw meets red cross on sill, faint dashed alternative paw target trajectory. Bottom small inset: curved cat-paw paint region next to a hatched protected windowsill region, teal nominal brush footprint constrained to intended paw side, curved boundary; labels 'Paw contour', 'Protected sill', 'Brush footprint'. This is conceptual geometric clipping, NOT a guarantee about every native brush fringe.
Column 3: '3 Paint editable parts'. Show the SAME posed cat as a cohesive softly painted grey/cream cat, natural face and clear contact with sill, gentle shadow. Below show four compact aligned transparent checkerboard layer thumbnails, named 'Head', 'Raised foreleg', 'Body', 'Tail'. Each thumbnail shows ONLY that component at its correct position in the SAME cat coordinate frame; all thumbnails together reconstruct the visible cat, no extra complete cat on a single thumbnail. Head includes ears and eyes as simple illustrative detail, not a claim of exhaustive minimum layer granularity. Label stack 'Separate raster layers'. Each example layer may require many strokes. Do not show the cat holding a pen or painting anything.
Bottom feedback arrow from right to left labelled exactly 'Inspect the rendered pixels'. Bottom caveat exactly 'Solved constraints are not proof of anatomy or artistic quality.' Small bottom-right footer 'Conceptual engineering diagram'. Do not add other text, logo, robotic actuator, fake measurements, mandatory serial-method arrows, unconnected technical props, or decorative gradients.

Title: 'WHEN THE REPLY IS LOST, RECOVER THE EVIDENCE'

Layout: clean left-to-right incident path along the top: 'Submit operation' → 'Photoshop may execute' → 'Reply lost'. Below these cards draw a neatly spaced fork with four equally valid outcomes labelled 'Completed', 'Not executed', 'Partial', 'Still uncertain'. From Completed and Not executed route toward a common rightmost card 'Next authorized action'; from Partial route to a separate amber card 'Bounded recovery'; from Still uncertain route to a separate amber card 'Keep blocked'. Small footer note at bottom left: 'No new paint until the state is confirmed.' Include simple disk/receipt/frame icons only. Do not imply that every outage is automatically resolved, that a receipt proves visual quality, that partial execution is safe to replay, or that a checkpoint is always current. All connectors must have a clear source and destination; use no looping arrows that could be interpreted as automatic paint retry.
